Birthday Party Checklist

A great birthday party is really just a handful of things done on time — the invites out early, the cake ordered, and the space ready before the first guest knocks. This checklist covers the essentials for a kids' or adult birthday so nothing slips through the cracks. Use it as-is, or open it in Gisti to tick things off, and browse the rest of our party and event checklists.

verified Curated by the Gisti team · Updated July 2026

Birthday Party Checklist · 16 items

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Set the date, start and end time, and a rough guest count
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Set a budget and split it across food, cake, decor, and entertainment
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Pick a theme or color scheme

    A theme makes every other choice — invites, decor, cake — easier.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Choose and book the venue, or prep your home

    Book venues 4 to 6 weeks ahead; popular kids' spots go fast on weekends.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Send invitations 3 to 4 weeks ahead with an RSVP date

    A clear RSVP date lets you finalize food and favor counts.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Plan the menu: food, drinks, and any dietary or allergy needs
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Order or bake the cake, and buy candles and a lighter

    Confirm any allergy-safe cake needs when you order.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Plan decorations: balloons, banner, tablecloth, and centerpieces
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Plan activities and entertainment: games, a playlist, or a photo backdrop
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Buy party favors or goodie bags
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Buy or wrap the birthday gift
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Stock disposables: plates, cups, napkins, utensils, and trash bags
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Prep a music playlist and test the speaker
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Charge your phone or camera for photos
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Day-of: set up 1 to 2 hours early, chill the drinks, and set out food just before guests arrive
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Assign someone to greet guests and someone to manage the cake and candles moment

    You'll want a free hand to actually enjoy it.

Frequently asked questions

How far in advance should I plan a birthday party? expand_more

Start about 4 to 6 weeks out. Book the venue and send invitations 3 to 4 weeks ahead so guests can RSVP, then handle the cake, decor, and favors in the final two weeks. A milestone party with a big guest list needs a longer runway.

How much food should I plan for a birthday party? expand_more

Plan roughly 6 to 8 small bites or appetizer portions per person for a 2 to 3 hour party, plus cake. If it spans a mealtime, plan a full meal instead. Always over-cater slightly on drinks and add a non-alcoholic option for every guest.

What do people forget when planning a birthday party? expand_more

The most-forgotten items are candles and a lighter, enough ice, trash bags, serving utensils, and a phone charger for photos. It also helps to assign someone to handle the cake moment so the host isn't juggling matches and a camera at once.
